factions.name: Felid Corsairs
factions.founding_event: The Long Run — 300 years ago, a stray uprising in the slums of port Ninth Gutter led to a mass exodus of unregistered alley cats from the oppressive Lion caste system. They stole decommissioned merchant ships and fled into the Fringe.
factions.founding_figure: Tessera the Uncounted — a three-legged stray matriarch who refused every name a Lion had given her. She organised the Strays, led the Long Run, and built the Corsairs' meritocratic culture deliberately opposed to everything the Lions represented.
factions.living_memory: Every Corsair captain knows the story of the Long Run. The Lions remember it as a rebellion. The Corsairs remember it as an escape. Both are right. Aristotle is the ninth generation of the Long Run, descended from Tessera through his mother's line — though he does not know it.

abilities.name: Crystal Refining
abilities.description: Only faction that can refine raw crystals, increasing quality grade

abilities.name: Shadow Running
abilities.description: Ships evade detection in hostile territory

abilities.name: Cunning Diplomacy
abilities.description: Unlocks bluff/misdirect dialogue options in diplomatic encounters

factions.name: Canis League
factions.founding_event: The Crystal Famine — two centuries ago, a major supply route collapse caused millions of dogs to starve. General Howl organised surviving packs into a cooperative militia that secured supply routes and distributed food fairly. Forty years after her death, the aristocratic Venator family captured the League from within: they centralised command, absorbed the Wolves as a 'military elite,' and rewrote the founding documents to emphasise obedience over loyalty.
factions.founding_figure: General Howl — a working-class mastiff who believed pack loyalty was the only moral force strong enough to prevent famine. Her original charter is still preserved in a sealed archive. Dave has read it. So has Charlie. It is one of the reasons Dave's loyalty crisis is possible.
factions.origin_era: 200 years ago (Howl's founding); 160 years ago (Venator coup)
factions.living_memory: Dave and Charlie both know what the League was supposed to be. Admiral Venator is the great-great-granddaughter of the man who ruined it. Brigadier Jessamine Howl is the great-great-granddaughter of the woman who built it.

abilities.name: Organised Warfare
abilities.description: Fleet formations grant +15% armour when 2+ League ships present

abilities.name: Siege Tactics
abilities.description: Can blockade supply routes, reducing crystal throughput by 50%

abilities.name: Superior Logistics
abilities.description: Resupply and repair at League ports costs 20% less

factions.name: The Lions
factions.founding_event: The Lion civilisation predates crystal-burning by a hundred thousand years, organised around the Prides — extended family dynasties descending from the Twelve Manes. The current crisis: Crown Prince Thorold, the beloved progressive heir, was poisoned at a state dinner. His younger brother Rhodion inherited both his reform agenda and a burning need to find the killer. The resulting civil war splits the Shattered Prides.
factions.founding_figure: The Twelve Manes — mythological founding kings who, according to Lion legend, tamed the first jump gates with a roar. (The gates were actually made by Solenne, but the Lions never met her.) Lord Mane's given name is Rhodion of House Amber; he took the title 'Mane' as a claim after Thorold's murder.
factions.living_memory: The Lions have never quite forgiven the universe for changing under them. Lady Penumbra (real name: Obsidia Vale) is a Black Cat of the exiled night-court tradition, using the civil war to settle a forty-year family vendetta. Blood Paw knows who poisoned Thorold.

abilities.name: Diplomatic Pressure
abilities.description: Force tribute demands costing crystals if refused, worsening reputation

abilities.name: Noble Authority
abilities.description: Lion presence in a region grants +20% political influence over neutral factions

abilities.name: Royal Decree
abilities.description: Can temporarily close trade routes to factions they are hostile toward

factions.name: The Wolves
factions.founding_event: The defence of Drennhal — a hundred years ago, an alien incursion threatened the Wolf homeworld. The original Iron Fang, a Wolf matriarch, led the planetary defence and repelled the invaders. The current Iron Fang is the sixth of the line to bear that name — a large, tired male who wears it like an inherited debt.
factions.founding_figure: Iron Fang I — the matriarch who saved Drennhal. Her name became a title, a burden, and an impossible standard. Wolf culture coalesced around The Hunt Eternal: every generation must outdo the last. It produces extraordinary soldiers and miserable individuals.
factions.origin_era: 100 years ago (current cultural form); ancient homeworld pre-spaceflight
factions.living_memory: Wolf suicide rates are the highest in the multiverse. Wolf poetry — which exists — is almost uniformly about exhaustion. The current Iron Fang has a daughter named Kestrel (16) who hates the Hunt Eternal and is already plotting her escape. Luna is Iron Fang's niece.

abilities.name: Tactical Superiority
abilities.description: Wolf ships gain +20% firepower when initiating combat (first-strike)

abilities.name: Pack Coordination
abilities.description: Multiple Wolf ships share targeting data, reducing player dodge chance by 15%

abilities.name: Evolutionary Right
abilities.description: Diplomatic encounters can escalate to combat with no reputation penalty

factions.name: Fairies
factions.founding_event: The Fairies remember Solenne — the last Builder who stayed behind to tend the crystal garden. Their civilisation is built around a living archive called the Heart Garden, a pocket dimension full of crystalline flowers that record everything spoken near them. Some of the oldest flowers still hum with Solenne's voice.
factions.founding_figure: Ember-Who-Remembers — not a committee but a single individual reflected across twelve bodies. She has been searching for a crystal steward for a thousand years. She chose Aristotle because he apologised to a crystal before using it. (This happens in a single unvoiced gesture in Arc 1. Silky saw it.)
factions.origin_era: Ancient — Fairies witnessed Solenne and the earliest crystal cultivation
factions.living_memory: Fairies do not reproduce — they bud. Every living fairy carries scraps of every fairy who came before. Fairy elders do not grieve death the way others do. Pip the Cartographer carries a memory she does not understand — a fragment of Solenne's final words. Moth holds the oldest crystal fragment, containing a recording of Solenne's voice.

abilities.name: Magical Espionage
abilities.description: Reveal hidden story flags or NPC true states for a crystal fee

abilities.name: Enchanted Goods
abilities.description: Fairy trade items grant temporary stat buffs lasting 3 encounters

abilities.name: Intelligence Networks
abilities.description: Purchasing fairy intel reveals encounter tables for the current region

factions.name: Knights
factions.founding_event: The Cordance Massacre — four hundred years ago, the realm of Cordance was devastated by a Lion punitive expedition over a tribute dispute. The survivors — a mixed population of badgers, otters, and other species — swore that never again would chaos tear their world apart. They organised around the Last Dawn Oath: order, honour, and mutual obligation above all else.
factions.founding_figure: The founders of the Order of the Last Dawn — no single named figure, but the survivors of Cordance collectively. Ser Galvain is the current Grand Marshal: a badger, not a cat or dog, who lost his own family in a minor raid thirty years ago and has been married to the Oath ever since.
factions.living_memory: The Knights' rigidity is a trauma response — every Knight has been told since childhood that order is the only thing standing between civilisation and another Cordance. Thistle (real name Briar Galvain) is Ser Galvain's estranged niece. Brother Ashen is beginning to wonder whether the Oath can survive contact with a multiverse that has moved on.

abilities.name: Heavy Armour
abilities.description: Knight crew members grant +10% armour to any ship they serve on

abilities.name: Disciplined Formations
abilities.description: Knight-allied fleet combat reduces incoming damage by 10%

abilities.name: Siege Engineering
abilities.description: Can breach blockaded routes at reduced cost

factions.name: Goblins
factions.founding_event: No founding myth — Goblins do not believe in myths. Their civilisation emerged from a federation of scrap-scavenging crews who figured out that fixing broken things was more profitable than stealing working ones. The Goblin Warrens are governed by rotating 'Deal Chiefs' elected by showing the largest profit margin of the previous cycle.
factions.founding_figure: Madam Sprocket — current Deal Chief, who made her fortune selling decommissioned League warships back to the League under different paint jobs. Has seven children, all running rival trading houses. Most goblins Aristotle meets are some flavour of Sprocket relative — the clan has been manoeuvring to get close to Aristotle since they heard about refined crystals.
factions.origin_era: Unknown — goblins do not track history, they track margins
factions.living_memory: Goblins will cheat you if they can, then buy you a drink if the cheat was clever. Yarrow is the only goblin who refuses to sell out — a pariah in goblin society, secretly the most reliable goblin in the story.

abilities.name: Rapid Ship Modification
abilities.description: Goblin engineers can apply upgrades mid-encounter (emergency repairs)

abilities.name: Black-Market Crystal Trade
abilities.description: Buy/sell crystals outside normal trade channels at volatile prices

abilities.name: Sabotage Services
abilities.description: Hire goblins to reduce a target faction's military_strength or internal_stability

factions.name: Aliens & Space Races
factions.founding_event: Not a single faction — a loose coalition of ancient species who share one priority: preventing the crystal network from dying. They have been trying for millions of years. They have been failing for just as long. They have watched a hundred potential stewards rise and fall across eons.
factions.founding_figure: The Void Singer — not a species but a position. When one Void Singer dies, another takes the role. The current one is a column of drifting light, was once a physical creature from a planet that no longer exists, has been the Void Singer for sixty thousand years.
factions.origin_era: Millions of years — ancient preservation coalition predating most current civilisations
factions.living_memory: The aliens are not hostile, but they are desperate. Aristotle is not their first choice as steward — he is their latest choice. They are running out of choices. Kiln is the alien who speaks normally, with humour and weariness — the alien you can have dinner with.

abilities.name: Superior Technology
abilities.description: Alien weapons ignore 25% of target armour

abilities.name: Unknown Weapons
abilities.description: Alien combat encounters have unpredictable damage variance (±50%)

abilities.name: Deeply Unpredictable Behaviour
abilities.description: Alien diplomatic outcomes have a random modifier that can swing results ±20%
